class_layout.pad_note: the +8..+0x113 gap is written as char pad[0x10c] purely so the CoordinateFrame lands on +0x114 (4 bytes of context at +4, then 0x114-8 = 0x10c bytes). No method written so far touches that range; a future port that needs those bytes must derive their meaning from the binary, not from this padding.
class_layout.alignment_trap: my first attempt used pad[0x110] and scored 97 with the only difference inside the lea displacement - 0x118 instead of 0x114. Cheap reminder that a padding arithmetic slip shows up as a 1-byte mismatch, not a size mismatch.
class_layout.sizeof_note: RBX::TextureProxyBase measures 0x28 in this unit (a byte-offset-aligned diff showed my first stand-in pushing operator new(0x84) instead of 0x60, which pinned sizeof(base) == 0x28 exactly). The vendor RbxGraphics/TextureProxyBase.h declares no data members of its own, so the 0x28 comes from G3D::ReferenceCountedObject and whatever the shared RbxGraphics/Adorn.h pulls in. AdornRbxGfxTexture therefore needs char pad[0x38], not the 0x5c a naive vptr-only reading would suggest - the same lesson as the AdornRbxGfx +0x114 padding slip: derive sizes from a measured compile, never from an assumed base.

get2DStringBounds 0066fe30.body_written: G3D::Vector2 AdornRbxGfx::get2DStringBounds(const std::string& s, double size, Adorn::Spacing spacing) const { return currentFont->get2DStringBounds(s, size, static_cast<G3D::GFont::Spacing>(spacing)); } - the call chain is right (the global font at 0x962dac, the double spilled as the 4th argument, the sret), so only the RETURN differs.
get2DStringBounds 0066fe30.residual: the original does NOT forward the outer sret to the callee. It passes a separate stack buffer as the callee's sret and then copies the two floats back one at a time through the x87 (fld [local]; fstp [outer sret]; fld [local+4]; fstp [outer sret+4]). MSVC does the same forwarding for mine, which is where the 13 bytes go.
get2DStringBounds 0066fe30.mined_reference: src/2008-06/0066fe30.cpp (100% by king_originala) expresses it as an explicit sret parameter plus a temporary that is filled and then copied - Size* measure(Size* result, const Text* text, double height, int mode) { Size* temporary = reinterpret_cast<Size*>(&height); currentFont->measure(temporary, text, height, mode); result->x = temporary->x; result->y = temporary->y; return result; }
get2DStringBounds 0066fe30.next: port the reference body verbatim from src/2008-06/0066fe30.cpp: it spells the callee with an explicit sret parameter (Size* result) and fills a temporary that aliases the double's stack slot, then copies two floats. Doing that in this unit means declaring the unnamed callee 0x684640 with the explicit-sret shape, which is a stand-in binding rather than a named G3D entry point - so it is an owner call whether to adopt the stand-in or keep the honest 43 B form.

rect2d_note: rect2d was exact on the first attempt once the members were named. It calls getHeight() TWICE (vtable slot 6, eax+0x18) with a `dec eax` after each giving (height()-1), flips the y coordinates by subtracting them, and passes the 28-byte std::string member at +8 BY VALUE plus a 9-float tail (x0, y0', x1, y1', 0, 0, 1, 1) to a renderer reached through [this+4] at +0x14. G3D::Rect2D exposes x0/y0/x1/y1 as ACCESSOR METHODS, not fields - writing rect.x0 is a C3867 error.
hoisting_lesson: naming the context members (context->viewport) initially BROKE getViewport: 160 B instead of 148, because MSVC re-loaded the pointer for each of the four getActual* calls instead of hoisting it once. The fix is a hoisted local - `const void* viewport = context->viewport;` - which is both byte-exact and still readable. A raw-offset read written inline happened to force the hoist, so the raw form looked "more exact" for a misleading reason.
